findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (which the installed-calendars page does not pass). Unlike `disconnectMutation`, it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. After the user confirms deletion, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated" and the "Delete cached data" item (derived from the now-stale `cacheUpdatedAt`) until a full refetch, so the action appears to have had no effect and can be re-triggered against an already-empty cache.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, reporting expired cache as live
findings.body: The `groupBy` only filters on `credentialId` and takes `_max(updatedAt)`. Rows whose `expiresAt` is in the past are still returned, so the UI will display a "Cache Status: Last updated …" for a credential whose cache is no longer served by `getCachedAvailability` (which does filter `expiresAt >= now`). The status shown to users is therefore misleading; the query should include `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` or report expiry explicitly.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars, but nothing consumes them
findings.body: The `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` picks were widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Only `findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated to select those columns; any other caller that builds a `UserWithCalendars` (platform API v2, other repository paths selecting a subset of SelectedCalendar fields) will now fail type-checking or need extra data fetched. Nothing in this PR reads these fields (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache), so this is an unnecessary contract tightening with breakage risk; it should be reverted or the fields made optional.

findings.title: Extra updateMany on every cache refresh with no consumer
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now issues `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {})` on every webhook/cron refresh solely to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The PR itself notes the frontend does not use this value (it uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`). This adds a write touching every SelectedCalendar row for the credential on each refresh, with no functional benefit. Also, the `data` parameter is typed as `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` (which includes relation fields) while `updateMany` accepts `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`; the types should match.

findings.title: Authorization failure throws a plain Error, surfacing as a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
findings.body: When the credential does not belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError` with code `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`. tRPC maps unknown errors to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so clients cannot distinguish an authorization failure from a server fault and the message is swallowed in production. Use `TRPCError` as other handlers in this router tree do.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to the en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` is used regardless of the user's locale, so non-English users get US-formatted dates (e.g. 7/15/25) inside an otherwise translated string. The component already has `useLocale()` available; the user's locale (or `i18n.language`) should be passed to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and the .env path is relative to the working directory
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed syntax; on GNU sed (Linux) `-i ''` is parsed as an empty in-place suffix followed by `''` as the script, causing "unknown command" and leaving `.env` unmodified. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's cwd rather than the script location, so running from the repo root writes to a `.env` outside the repository. Also `cleanup` always `exit 0`, so the failure paths (rate limit, no URL) report success to callers.

findings.title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script was changed from `ts-node` (a declared devDependency) to `npx tsx`, but `tsx` is not added to devDependencies. `npx` will fall back to downloading an arbitrary latest version at runtime (and may prompt interactively), making the script non-reproducible and failing in offline/CI environments. Either add `tsx` to devDependencies or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the PR's feature.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache handler or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
findings.body: The PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCacheHandler`) with an ownership check and a new repository aggregation (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`) but includes no unit or integration tests. In particular the authorization path (another user's credentialId must be rejected) and the mapping of credentialId → updatedAt in `connectedCalendarsHandler` are untested; the PR description itself notes end-to-end verification could not be performed.
